summary: A serious race-day commitment or an unusual spectator outing on Sunday 20 December 2026. The full marathon starts at Tha Phae Gate at 03:00 and finishes in Mae Rim, so supporters must choose between the atmospheric city start and a separate finish-line trip.
whyGo: Combine a trained-for marathon with a Chiang Mai holiday.
Watch runners set off beside the Old City gate, or support a friend at the Mae Rim finish.
bestFor: Prepared distance runners who can reserve time for recovery.
Supporters willing to plan an early start and a separate meeting point.
skipIf: You have not trained for a full marathon; choose a shorter distance or spectate.
You want a convenient city-centre finish or a spontaneous late-morning outing.
duration: Runners have seven hours before the 10:00 cutoff; allow staging, return travel and recovery too. For spectators, budget 45–90 minutes at one location as a planning estimate.
cost: Foreign marathon entry: THB1,500 through 31 October; THB2,000 on 1–20 November; THB2,500 on 1–15 December, plus processing fees. Spectator charges are not published; budget separately for transport.
hours: Race: 20 December 2026, 03:00 start and 10:00 cutoff. Marathon bag transfer: 02:00–02:50. Bib collection: 18–19 December, 10:00–18:00 at Tha Phae Gate.
bestTime: Stay within walking distance of the start if racing. Spectators should choose the start for atmosphere or the finish around their runner’s predicted arrival.
gettingThere: Start: Tha Phae Gate. Finish: King Naresuan the Great Monument, Mae Rim. Free runner return shuttles run 06:30–10:30. Supporter access to those shuttles is unconfirmed; arrange independent transport if heading to Mae Rim.
booking: Enter via the official website’s registration link and collect your bib in advance. Fees are non-refundable. Check availability before booking travel. Watching arrangements and any restricted finish areas need reconfirmation.
accessibility: Wheelchair entry, accessible spectator areas, toilets and shuttle boarding have not been confirmed. Contact the organiser before relying on specific facilities.
practicalTips: Agree an exact meeting point and carry a charged phone; start and finish are different locations.
Supporters should carry water and breakfast and allow for road closures.
Keep the afternoon flexible for rest; avoid scheduling a strenuous excursion after racing.
decemberNotes: Confirmed for December 2026. The organiser describes a flat route and cool conditions, but its temperature range is promotional guidance rather than a forecast. Check final weather and race instructions shortly before departure.
uncertainties: Final road closures, spectator facilities and transport eligibility remain unconfirmed.
Remaining entry availability and accessible arrangements were not verified.
The photograph shows a historical edition, not the 2026 course or staging.
